votes.lens: Autonomy integrity — can this actually run with zero human minutes on the unhappy paths (ambiguous input, stale corpus, angry customer, refund/chargeback, legal exposure), judged against 12-Factor App and Karpathy on LLM systems
votes.rationale:
Judged on whether autonomy survives the unhappy path, not on how many fail-closed sentences a pitch contains.

Sunset Graph leads because it exports verification: the customer's own CI adjudicates every codemod, so Karpathy's generation-verification loop closes without an operator, and the corpus is entirely versioned machine artifacts (SDL, OpenAPI, endoflife.date — 83KB JSON, verified live). A bad output is a closed PR, not a fine. Rate Card is the purest 12-Factor build — no LLM in the money path, a golden-canary invoice gating deploys (dev/prod parity), Stripe auto-credit on Partial runs — docked because card-statement geometry is a standing parsing tax and a null $149 teardown is a refund conversation. Ship Record designs the money unhappy path end to end (UNWATCHED banner plus auto-credit), though subprocessor pages behind bot walls quietly shrink coverage. Wage Line's arithmetic is the most deterministic here and its FAR 22.404-6 refusal the pool's most honest boundary, but failing closed against an undocumented SAM endpoint on a Friday statutory deadline manufactures precisely the angry customer for whom it declares no support path. Portfolio Guard's clause→observable-fact join is permanent human editorial work, and Apple/Google enforcement is discretionary, not a function of a published page. Landed's sources really are APIs (HTS reststop returned JSON), yet its headline liability number hinges on a future Commerce decision. Allowed Amount carries terabyte per-payer ingest against CRS-documented bad data — engineering minutes forever. Redlist last: both corpora are HTML-only (verified — no API; FDA 302s), and its crown jewel is LLM extraction of ppm limits from legal PDFs.

votes.lens: PMF evidence: Mom Test (real money/behaviour beats stated interest), Ellis 40% rule, Andreessen market pull — ranked by strength of proof that money already changes hands for a worse solution to the same job.
votes.rationale: Mom Test evidence means a named vendor cashing a named check for a worse version of the same job. Wage Line wins outright: contractors pay LCPtracker/eBacon $175–$1,200/mo plus $995–$4,995 setup — nobody pays four-figure onboarding out of curiosity — and the substitute is ~$19,500/yr of clerical labour already funded. Andreessen pull is structural: the GC will not release payment without a defensible WH-347. Rate Card is second on cash velocity: LateShipment already takes 25–35% of recoveries, the purest revealed preference here. Discount it, though — contingency converts because nothing leaves the buyer's pocket, and Swipesum/FeeQuery giving statement analysis away free prices the diagnostic at zero; the beachhead is deliberately below where Sifted or Shipware quote, so pull is proven one tier up, not in-segment. Ship Record third: FOSSA at ~$207 and sbomify at $159 are money moving for attribution today, but the CRA half is a September 2026 deadline, and anticipated compliance is stated interest until the first fine lands. Portfolio Guard's Opteo/Optmyzr/WP Remote comparables prove agencies buy software, not that anyone buys policy monitoring — today's incumbent is a free Google email. Redlist's $10k–$90k settlements flow to plaintiffs' counsel, and it concedes purchase is trigger-driven; Ellis's 40% needs habitual use. Allowed Amount and Landed both confess non-purchase in their own copy — pharmacies "never executed the appeal," importers "reserve nothing" — and Landed skips the crowded paid end for the unpaid one. Sunset Graph rests on HN comments against free Dependabot: pain stated, never purchased.

votes.lens: speed-to-revenue-selfserve — Ries lean MVP with the concierge shortcut banned: how fast can a fully automated v1 be built and charge a real credit card, judged on ingestion friction, pre-revenue corpus burden, determinism of the output, external human gates, and whether the buyer purchases without a call.
votes.rationale: Ries's MVP test here is build-time to a charged card, so I discount every Helmer moat that must be assembled before v1 emits anything. Rate Card wins: ingestion is a file the customer already owns (UPS Billing Data export) — no OAuth, no API approval, no scraping exposure — the recompute is arithmetic with no LLM in the money path, and the pure error findings (address correction $25.50, DIM, residential misclass) compute without contract rates, so the $149 teardown ships before the effective-dated rulebook is finished. Dunford's flat-fee-not-contingency line removes a buying objection rather than adding a concept. Ship Record is second: SPDX license-list-data and KEV/OSV are free and structured, the CRA 11 September clock is four weeks out, and FOSSA/sbomify bracket a proven self-serve price. Wage Line's WH-347 math and PDF are bounded, but eCPR XSD conformance is untestable without a DIR account and the $49 rate card is free public data reformatted. Redlist's $199 category report needs only the AG notice mirror, but both corpora are HTML scrapes with no API and settlement-PDF ppm extraction is a research project. Portfolio Guard is gated on Google Ads developer-token approval — a human external dependency that breaks the automated premise — atop a hand-authored clause-to-fact join. Sunset Graph needs four language surface-diff toolchains and sandboxed test-gated codemods before Moore's beachhead pays. Landed's fast half, classification, is commoditized by Zonos/3CE; its wedge, the AD/CVD rate graph, is the slow half. Allowed Amount is last: terabyte MRF ingest plus healthcare's slowest buyers, even at Ramanujam-friendly $149.

votes.lens: Willingness to pay and monetization clarity — Ramanujam (WTP-first, value metric, packaging, price ceiling), Hormozi (value equation, risk reversal), Poyar/OpenView (value-metric alignment, expansion/NDR, self-serve price bands). Ranked by price ceiling defensibility for a no-human product.
votes.rationale: Ramanujam's WTP-first test: is the budget already forced, and does a reference price exist? Wage Line leads — WH-347 filing is legally mandatory weekly, DBA penalties run $28,619/violation plus FCA trebling, and it emits the filed artifact (PDF plus XSD-validated eCPR XML), which is what carries Hormozi's perceived-likelihood term; the per-report metric is market-validated. Skeptical hit: I verified CertifiedPayrollPro already sells self-serve at $49–$249/mo plus $1–5/report with no setup fee, so "zero setup fee is the wedge" is occupied — the premium must come from the WD revision-history corner, not from price. Landed second: I found no self-serve AD/CVD comparable (Descartes-class is quote-only), so $899 against six-figure retroactive liquidation sets its own anchor, with the >20%-unresolved auto-refund as genuine Hormozi risk reversal. Caveat — no reference price also means unproven budget. Allowed Amount and Portfolio Guard own the best Poyar value metrics (NPIs aggregated via RCM resellers; accounts × managed spend), yet both self-cap: $149–$399 chosen explicitly to dodge physician sign-off, and I confirmed Opteo at $129/$249/$499 for 10/25/75 accounts — the market has already priced that exact metric low. Ship Record splits three jobs across no single metric against FOSSA's $207 and free SBOM tooling, then hits an urgency trough between Sept 2026 and Dec 2027. Rate Card has the clearest ROI and worst ceiling: LateShipment charges 25–35% contingency — $0 upfront — so flat $149 fights a zero-risk alternative while forfeiting all upside. Redlist confesses trigger-driven churn. Sunset Graph substitutes $700/engineer-day labour against free Dependabot for the pool's poorest buyers.

votes.lens: Moat and retention: compounding, time-locked or usage-fed data advantage (Helmer 7 Powers, Thiel proprietary tech) combined with habitual, high-frequency use and automatic expansion (Vohra Superhuman PMF, Poyar frequency/NRR). One-off transactional jobs rank low.
votes.rationale: Wage Line wins both axes. A legally compelled weekly WH-347 is the highest-frequency habit here (Poyar), and the payroll-title→SOC→WD-class crosswalk is the pool's only asset compounding from customer corrections rather than crawling — real Thiel proprietary tech atop a WD revision history SAM.gov won't bulk-export (Helmer cornered resource). Vohra's 40% test passes trivially when Friday's filing gates payment. Allowed Amount: payers overwrite MRFs and CMS ships snapshots, not changelogs, so the longitudinal series is genuinely unreconstructable; terabyte ingest is a scale economy; Turquoise's cannibalization fear is real counter-positioning. But alerting is ambient, not obligatory, and RCM resale, not habit, supplies NRR. Portfolio Guard has the best NRR mechanic — accounts and spend metered from the API — and a buyer living in those accounts daily; yet policy pages are cheap to crawl, only diff history is locked, and Opteo/Optmyzr sit adjacent. Sunset Graph is the most workflow-embedded (push webhooks, PRs) and surface-diffing is genuine proprietary tech, but npm/PyPI artifacts are immutable, so a later entrant re-derives that half retroactively; "cannot backfill" is half-true, and Dependabot is free. Ship Record's per-release SBOMs and LICENSE history are rebuildable from git, and CRA demand is deadline-shaped — latent after September. Landed's AD/CVD graph is strong assembly, but its recurring event is an annual review anniversary, and it concedes classification, the sticky part. Redlist names its own defect — trigger-driven purchase, hostile to renewal — despite the best cornered resource. Rate Card last: a $149 one-shot whose value self-terminates once the leak is fixed; flat-fee positioning is copyable in a week.

votes.lens: Distribution without a salesperson — strength of compounding self-serve channels (Weinberg & Mares Bullseye, Hormozi Core Four minus human selling): programmatic SEO, app stores/marketplaces, communities, integrations, free tools
votes.rationale: Bullseye (Weinberg & Mares) rewards breadth then concentration; Hormozi's Core Four minus human selling leaves cold content, free tools, marketplaces, integrations. Sunset Graph alone hits four: GitHub Marketplace, the GitHub App as channel-and-integration, HN/Shopify-Partner communities that adopt dev tools without a call, and a free single-repo scan whose output — a draft PR — every engineer in the repo sees, the pool's only in-org viral loop. Discount its SEO; endoflife.date already owns those queries, free. Redlist has the deepest programmatic asset: tens of thousands of notice, defendant, plaintiff-firm and import-alert pages over a corpus with no API or export, matched to the panic query — your own company name, the day the letter lands. Second only because it is single-channel and itself admits trigger-driven purchase. Ship Record stacks three link-earning free tools, but the CRA hook decays past 11 Sept 2026 and the subprocessor-feed reader isn't reliably the buyer. Wage Line has the best free-tool-to-product intent match (WH-347 generator) plus a county×craft long tail — but davisbaconrates.com sits in its own evidence list, there's no marketplace or integration, and it leans on SAM.gov cold lists into a demo-and-quote buyer. Landed's Shopify listing and HTS pages feed classification, the commodity it concedes isn't the wedge, while AD/CVD importers arrive via broker BD. Portfolio Guard's digest compounds across only a few hundred policy pages. Rate Card owns one calculator on SERPs saturated by contingency lead-gen. Allowed Amount last: AMA licensing bars publishing the CPT descriptors its SEO needs, no store or integration exists, and its named route is reselling through billing companies — partnership selling by a human.
